title: From Analytic Structure to Quantum Complexity: Walsh-Pauli Representations of Continuum Operators
authors: Raphael De Sousa, Partha Nandi, Francesco Petruccione
abstract: How does continuum operator structure appear in a finite qubit register? We address this question for analytic functions of diagonal operators represented in a binary basis, focusing on the Jordan--Lee--Preskill (JLP) momentum operator, by developing an operator-level generating-function framework for their Walsh-Pauli spectra. The construction determines the spectrum analytically and reveals exact support and parity selection rules, together with a nontrivial intra-shell hierarchy induced by the binary encoding. This provides a systematic characterization of Walsh compressibility and its relation to Pauli locality. As a controlled application, we consider generalized uncertainty-principle (GUP) kinematics as a tunable nonlinear odd deformation of momentum, showing how higher-order momentum terms redistribute spectral weight into progressively higher Pauli-weight sectors
summary: This work develops a systematic, analytical framework to translate the structure of continuum quantum operators into the discrete language of qubits using Walsh-Pauli representations. By employing generating functions, the authors determine the spectrum and resource cost associated with operators like the momentum operator, even when subjected to nonlinear deformations such as GUP kinematics. This offers a powerful preprocessing step for designing efficient quantum simulations.
main_problem: The paper addresses how the structure of a continuum operator, such as the momentum operator, is faithfully represented and characterized within a finite qubit register.
main_result: A generating-function framework is developed to analytically determine the Walsh-Pauli spectrum of analytic functions of the JLP momentum operator, revealing exact support and parity selection rules.
method: The core method involves mapping the continuum operator to a qubit-encoded operator, then using a generating function formalism to extract the Walsh-Pauli coefficients of the resulting function.
model_or_system: The model centers on the Jordan-Lee-Preskill (JLP) construction, which discretizes continuum degrees of freedom onto a finite qubit register. A controlled application is the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) kinematics, treated as a nonlinear deformation of momentum.
key_observables: Walsh-Pauli spectrum, Pauli-weight structure, Walsh compressibility, and estimated quantum circuit resource costs (e.g., CNOT gates).
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n_q$) defining the finite register size, and the deformation parameters characterizing the GUP.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to diagonal functions of a single JLP momentum register, and the method provides an upper bound for circuit costs.

paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the continuum-to-qubit mapping, developing the generating-function formalism for the spectrum, deriving selection rules (support/parity), and finally applying the framework to analyze physical deformations like GUP kinematics.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, analytical tool to estimate the quantum resources needed to simulate complex physical Hamiltonians (like those involving GUP) by analyzing the spectral structure of their momentum components.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic overview of the continuum-to-qubit con- struction developed in this work. The JLP encoding maps the continuum momentum to a binary qubit operator. An analytic function of the momentum operator is decomposed through a generating-function construction into Walsh–Pauli coefficients. The resulting spectrum determines the Pauli- weight structure and its compressibility, which are directly relevant for Pauli-string implementation and quantum-circuit resources. The quadratic GUP provides a concrete applica- tion of the general framework.
FIG. 3. Ratio Rw = W exact w /W LO w defined in Eq. (100). Values near unity indicate dominance of the leading Taylor contribution to the corresponding Pauli-weight shell.

FIG. 2. Exact Walsh shell weights of the quadratic-GUP operator compared with the leading-order analytical predic- tion Eq. (98) for nq = 8 and pmax ≈0.996. The agreement is excellent in the weak-deformation regime, while deviations appear as higher Taylor orders become appreciable.

FIG. 4. Discarded Walsh spectral fraction εD[kβ] = 1 − C(D), defined in Eqs. (101) and (102), as a function of the maximum retained Pauli weight D. Increasing the deforma- tion transfers spectral weight into higher-weight sectors and therefore increases the Pauli locality required at fixed accu- racy.

FIG. 5. Normalized Walsh shell weights for the representa- tive non-polynomial analytic deformations of Table II, evalu- ated on the same JLP momentum lattice at fixed deformation strength ϵ = βp2 max. All models populate only odd Pauli- weight sectors, reflecting their common parity, while the rel- ative distribution of spectral weight among the allowed shells depends on the analytic form of the deformation. The values shown are nq = 8, ϵ = 0.5 and pmax = 1.
